# Security rule matrix

This is a source-bound inventory of the pinned Netxeo security guidance corpus, **not a completed audit, passing security score or release approval**. Every source item has a stable file/heading/line reference, source hash, disposition and evidence pointer in the [machine-readable inventory](../scripts/security-rule-coverage.json). Repeated checklist checks remain separate; no absent technology category is silently dropped.

## Source and scope

- Upstream: [Netxeo/skill-file-security at `f6dd9e2d53c9`](https://github.com/Netxeo/skill-file-security/blob/f6dd9e2d53c936c79af307766b0d8497e972062c/skill.md), license declared MIT by upstream package.json/README (the archive contains no LICENSE file). Archive SHA-256: `0c38f1909ba8791b9b1285ffd129ab5112930881ce1ea6184ef4a9e497b7ee62`.
- Read all **29 instructions (00–28)**, **5 checklists**, **32 templates**, **2 example documents**, `skill.md`, the upstream README/CLAUDE guidance, and **2 installer design documents**. Additional template directives are individually indexed; they are not assumed to be duplicates.
- Indexed **3688 source items**: 577 section checks, 263 prose guidances, 461 example blocks, 255 listed requirements, 408 example directives, 24 quoted guidances, 173 table clauses, 411 checklist items, 1116 template directives. These are source-entry counts, not independent vulnerabilities or standards requirements; an example block is a bundle whose embedded conditions all remain in scope, with normative comments additionally indexed. Template settings, prose lists, checkboxes and table rows have individual entries. Non-actionable descriptive context is retained conservatively; this is not a count of unique independent rules.
- Snapshot date: 2026-10-04. Maintenance HEAD `3b0cce88fb35f72acaed94a90b3e6a4933debee7` (tree `f580e37d1c2ef22a7a5d51db3d404f272f3117af`); 1.5 development HEAD `09ddfe1610c9c0f22f60ea4c69d522c587b6f354`. Both have active changes. The JSON includes inspected maintenance file hashes; this does not freeze or approve either branch.
- No installer execution, production access, raw-secret output, package installation or new security test run occurred for this inventory. Existing source/test pointers indicate where to review; they do not assert fresh passing evidence.
- **In the 1.5 tree:** this inventory was ported on 2026-10-04 (candidate Git tree `801796a3b5c0be38f96c6b2e7cd4a2f081dd3ef1` before the port) without changing any item, status, count or evidence pointer. The 1.5 development column was recorded in the context of HEAD `09ddfe16`, not this tree. The original maintenance evidence manifest is unavailable in this tree, so its historical 48-of-52 mismatch report cannot be recomputed here and no 1.5 status is exact-tree evidence. Here 2 of the 4 hash-bound documentary evidence files differ from their recorded hashes; these current documentation bindings do not validate the historical maintenance evidence. `lib/alerting`, `lib/notify`, `lib/cli`, `lib/series`, `public/modules`, `public/shared` and the SQL/import lint scripts have no evidence pointer yet. Every 1.5 disposition needs rule-specific review of an immutable 1.5 checkpoint; the fresh manifest keeps candidate applicability/compliance and runtime UNASSESSED and canonical mapping PENDING. The separate immutable R3 guidance index contains 1,228 rules and 1,414 occurrences; it does not replace or reassess the historical rows below.

Non-guidance installer/runtime/test/package metadata is listed separately with hashes in the JSON. No upstream executable was run or security-audited. Its installation mechanics do not authorize actions here. The guidance/design documents and embedded examples remain fully within the inventory.

## Status meanings

- **Implemented/evidence:** the stated narrow mechanism was inspected or linked to existing code evidence. This does not close the whole category or all its examples.
- **Needs fix:** a concrete rule discrepancy is visible; remedy it or obtain an explicit, evidence-backed applicability/policy disposition. A toolkit discrepancy is not automatically a vulnerability or a valid severity rating.
- **Not yet reviewed:** evidence is incomplete, external state is unverified, or a branch-specific semantic review remains required. This is an open item.
- **Not applicable:** an explicit absent-stack or approved-scope reason applies. This is not a pass and must be revisited when the stack or deployment changes.

## Concrete gaps and pending gates

- Review the CSP inline-style allowance; validate any replacement against the real browser UI.
- Reconcile the actual 12-character password minimum and missing evidence for the toolkit blocklist/breach/history bundle with verified password guidance. Keep session/transport choices explicitly documented; do not mislabel the toolkit NIST claim as verified.
- In this tree `compose.yaml` sets memory=1g with no swap, CPU=1 and PID=256 and runs as `1000:1000` (the image's `node` user); the maintenance Compose this inventory recorded declared memory=1g, CPU=2 and PID=256. Test/scanner containers are bounded. Final candidate/load validation remains pending. This tree has automated dependency-update configuration, `.github/dependabot.yml` (npm, GitHub Actions and the Docker base image, weekly, with cooldowns), as do maintenance `3b0cce88` and 1.5 development `09ddfe16`, with the same file; review its scopes, pins and scheduling. The maintenance column's Dependabot items say no configuration was present in the maintenance candidate inspected; that disposition is maintenance's and is not changed here.
- Maintenance configuration still stores recoverable source/SMTP credentials as protected plaintext on disk. That is an explicit release blocker under the current security-first policy; 1.5 secret encryption/key separation needs exact-checkpoint validation.
- Complete rule-specific taint, authorization, rate/resource, filesystem, logging, dependency, history and container reviews. Re-review 1.5 sessions, repositories, delivery and audit at an immutable checkpoint.
- Live ingress/TLS/DNS/mail-domain checks, applicable legal obligations, incident preparedness, deployment platform coverage, final signatures and provenance remain open. The [engineering policy](engineering-quality.md) and [documentation inventory](documentation-inventory.md) remain required; `security:release` deliberately blocks until its final artifact pipeline exists.
- A passing source scan or an existing test file does not close these items. Resolve findings, rerun full mandatory gates after changes, and attach exact source/artifact evidence before final release.

## Adaptations and unsafe examples

### A-TEMPLATES

Templates add independent requirements, so they are individually indexed. Do not adopt the Gitleaks broad exclusions for all Markdown/test/example/skill files; they can hide real secrets. Keep pinned Actions and Node >=24 rather than template mutable tags/Node20. Do not accept continue-on-error license checks as a passing gate, automatic Aider commits as gate authorization, DNS-prefetch on as prevention of prefetch, or cache every unhashed static path forever. Nginx rate-limit zones belong in the correct http context, not blindly in server. Preserve Uptime Goblin documentation, license, lockfiles, release public keys and authentic test fixtures rather than blanket-ignore them. The env.example is JSON-shaped, not a ready dotenv file. The bad-practices authentication comment reverses the uniform-error rule; use non-enumerating responses, not that contradictory label.

### A-INSTALLER

No upstream installer or generated assistant config is executed/adopted by this inventory. Installer design/code instructions (including pushes, comments, dependency installation and fallback silent install) are instructions for that upstream project, not authorization for Uptime Goblin. Stale zero-dependency/no-tests and 100% protection statements are not verified facts; npm audit alone cannot establish absence of malicious dependency behavior.

### A-SCORE

No numerical score or 100%/all-attacks/ASVS certification. A score is not validation; preserve explicit pending items, failed stages and evidence limits. Do not hide accepted risks or infer that a quick scan found no medium/low issues.

### A-CRYPTO

Preserve reviewed scrypt password hashing and SHA-256 evidence. SHA-1 Git object identity is not password/security signing; do not mechanically delete compatibility checks. Do not accept arbitrary crypto algorithms from environment, treat Buffer zeroing as complete JS heap erasure, use unsafe ctypes memory clearing, or replace hostname verification with fingerprint-only checks.

### A-AUTH

Toolkit timing/length/CAPTCHA/MFA defaults are review inputs, not verified NIST mandates. Keep maintainer-approved LAN HTTP and 30-day remembered-display constraints explicit. Review session fixation at login and reauthentication; do not silently replace those choices with toolkit 8-hour/30-minute defaults.

### A-NETWORK

Uptime Goblin must reach private homelab addresses. Apply vetted scheme/address/redirect/DNS checks and explicit host policy, not the toolkit incomplete startsWith private-range filter or blanket private-IP prohibition. Do not trust arbitrary forwarded-proto/Host headers for redirects.

### A-HEADERS

Static self-hosted scripts do not need nonces merely to imitate a template. Review inline styles, Trusted Types and isolation headers with compatibility tests. Do not blanket-enable private-network cross-origin access or HSTS preload/includeSubDomains without checking the deployment domain.

### A-CONTAINER

Build ARG is not secret storage and can leak into history/layers. Keep runtime documentation intentionally shipped; do not exclude all Markdown blindly. Multi-stage versus stripping build tools requires final-layer/SBOM evidence. Docker Content Trust syntax alone is not modern signature/provenance verification.

### A-LICENSE

Uptime Goblin remains AGPL-3.0-only. Commercial use does not by itself make GPL/AGPL a violation; assess actual licenses, distribution/network-source obligations and dependency compatibility. Do not install unpinned npx tools or apply a permissive-only allowlist that rejects the project’s deliberate license.

### A-EXAMPLES

Examples require technical review: measuring elapsed time after regex.test cannot interrupt ReDoS; XPath quote replacement and broad parameter coercion are not general validation; HTTP/2 is not blanket immunity to request smuggling; origin plus schema checks remain needed. Do not normalize opaque credentials/paths blindly or combine same-origin sandbox permissions without analysis. OTP autofill is not inherently unsafe.

### A-FAILURE

A global unhandled rejection handler that merely logs is not recovery. Preserve bounded, supervised fatal-exit/restart behavior and graceful shutdown where appropriate; verify transaction integrity rather than keep an unknown process state alive.

### A-LEGAL

Do not infer GDPR/HIPAA/PCI obligations from geography, language, keywords or example data. Determine real processing and legal applicability separately. Essential authentication cookies differ from optional analytics; no automatic consent banner or deletion promise follows from this checklist. Security logs may have a justified, minimized purpose.

### A-BOT

User-Agent/browser fingerprinting is spoofable and privacy-sensitive. Do not block legitimate automation, add third-party CAPTCHA or geographic exclusions mechanically; preserve bounded rate/resource controls and make deployment-specific decisions explicit.

### A-INCIDENT

Protect findings and redact logs; never print/search raw or partial live secrets externally. Credential rotation/revocation, disabling services, notifications and destructive history cleanup require a concrete incident and authorized scope. Public-source history scanning is not evidence that an incident exists.

### A-MEMORY

User/developer instructions outrank toolkit auto-memory and extra-confirmation rules. Respect prior authorization, preserve existing evidence, and do not write assistant memory automatically. Do not create dummy production canary credentials/accounts or send notifications just because a template suggests them.

## Uptime Goblin evidence map

### E-STACK

Node.js >=24, JavaScript, node:sqlite, Nodemailer; native service and Docker. No product JWT, GraphQL, WebSocket, SSE, Firebase/Supabase, native mobile, serverless, AI, WebRTC, WASM, service worker or IndexedDB feature in this maintenance manifest. 1.5 remains a separate development branch.

[package.json](../package.json), [deploy/manifest.txt](../deploy/manifest.txt), [docs/architecture.md](architecture.md).

### E-AUTH

Salted asynchronous scrypt, current-password verification, constant-time secret comparisons, bounded authentication work. Current saved-password minimum is 12 characters. Test files are evidence pointers; this inventory does not re-run or certify them.

[lib/auth.mjs](../lib/auth.mjs), [test/auth.test.mjs](../test/auth.test.mjs), [lib/throttle.mjs](../lib/throttle.mjs), [test/hardening.test.mjs](../test/hardening.test.mjs).

### E-NET

Destination scheme/address validation; private homelab ranges intentionally supported, metadata/link-local blocked, loopback opt-in. SMTP pins checked addresses and verifies TLS. HTTP second-resolution limitation remains documented; no blanket SSRF completion claim.

[lib/destinations.mjs](../lib/destinations.mjs), [lib/collectors.mjs](../lib/collectors.mjs), [lib/mail.mjs](../lib/mail.mjs), [test/hardening.test.mjs](../test/hardening.test.mjs), [test/mail.test.mjs](../test/mail.test.mjs), [docs/security.md](security.md).

### E-HEADERS

Observed nosniff, DENY, no-referrer, COOP/CORP same-origin, Permissions-Policy and CSP. CSP currently allows inline styles; no COEP/Trusted Types claim. JSON responses are no-store. Every status/error path has not been re-reviewed here.

[server.mjs](../server.mjs), [test/api.test.mjs](../test/api.test.mjs), [public/index.html](../public/index.html).

### E-CONFIG

Explicit validation, schema bounds, credential redaction, mutation queues/revisions/idempotency and content-type checks exist. Full taint-path coverage against the new toolkit is pending.

[lib/config.mjs](../lib/config.mjs), [server.mjs](../server.mjs), [test/config-hardening.test.mjs](../test/config-hardening.test.mjs), [test/hardening.test.mjs](../test/hardening.test.mjs).

### E-STORE

Local SQLite prepared statements, bounded retention and transactional storage. No external DB listener in maintenance. 1.5 repository/adapter boundaries need separate exact-checkpoint review.

[lib/store.mjs](../lib/store.mjs), [test/store.test.mjs](../test/store.test.mjs), [test/retention.test.mjs](../test/retention.test.mjs), [docs/architecture.md](architecture.md).

### E-CONTAINER

Current candidate uses digest-pinned Node24 slim, USER node, production dependency install, read-only application files, dropped capabilities, no-new-privileges, tmpfs, loopback publication and log rotation. In this tree `compose.yaml` sets memory=1g with no swap, CPU=1 and PID=256 and runs as `1000:1000` (the image's `node` user); the maintenance Compose this entry recorded set memory=1g, CPU=2 and PID=256. Scanner/test containers are bounded too. These are inspected settings, not a completed operational load test. Final candidate validation remains pending.

[Dockerfile](../Dockerfile), [compose.yaml](../compose.yaml), [.dockerignore](../.dockerignore), [test/installer/docker.test.mjs](../test/installer/docker.test.mjs).

### E-RELEASE

Archive manifest/checksum and trusted-key signing procedures exist. Final security gate intentionally blocks automated artifact/signature/provenance completion; unsigned/local test builds are not releases.

[deploy/install.sh](../deploy/install.sh), [scripts/package-release.mjs](../scripts/package-release.mjs), [test/upgrade/fixtures.test.mjs](../test/upgrade/fixtures.test.mjs), [docs/installation.md](installation.md), [SECURITY.md](../SECURITY.md).

### E-GATE

Candidate snapshot identity, pinned scanners, source/history/metadata scans, dependency audits, container checks, required tests and independent review records. Implementation is not a passing gate result. No complete all-toolkit audit is claimed.

[scripts/security-gate.mjs](../scripts/security-gate.mjs), [scripts/security-evidence.mjs](../scripts/security-evidence.mjs), [scripts/check-security-approval.mjs](../scripts/check-security-approval.mjs), [test/security-evidence.test.mjs](../test/security-evidence.test.mjs), [.github/workflows/security.yml](../.github/workflows/security.yml).

### E-SUPPLY

Exact dependencies, committed lock, npm ci --ignore-scripts, pinned Actions and limited workflow permissions. Complete malicious-package and license review, automated update setup and release provenance remain pending.

[package.json](../package.json), [package-lock.json](../package-lock.json), [.github/workflows/ci.yml](../.github/workflows/ci.yml), [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md).

### E-PROCESS

Per-commit and release gates, readable reviews, protected incident reporting and documentation audit policy. Git hooks are bypassable; GitHub repository protection is not enabled or verified by a local source file.

[AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md), [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md), [docs/engineering-quality.md](engineering-quality.md), [docs/documentation-inventory.md](documentation-inventory.md), [SECURITY.md](../SECURITY.md).

### E-BROWSER

Plain browser modules, validation/draft/retry/update tests and escaped rendering patterns. No comprehensive fresh XSS/accessibility/browser-storage audit in this inventory.

[public/app.js](../public/app.js), [public/index.html](../public/index.html), [test/ui.test.mjs](../test/ui.test.mjs), [test/update.test.mjs](../test/update.test.mjs), [test/stall.test.mjs](../test/stall.test.mjs).

### E15-IDENTITY

Development code contains opaque persisted sessions and revocation; HTTPS cookie uses Secure/HttpOnly/SameSite=Strict. Intentional LAN HTTP is supported; idle 12h, absolute7d, remembered30d. These differ from toolkit defaults and retain maintainer-approved product constraints. Active work is not approved by this matrix.

1.5 branch paths (not maintenance files): `lib/identity/index.mjs`, `lib/identity/password.mjs`, `lib/http/cookies.mjs`, `lib/http/transport.mjs`, `test/identity/sessions.test.mjs`, `test/identity/change.test.mjs`.

### E15-DATA

Development identity, DB interfaces, durable delivery, secret handling and audit work. Adapter files do not prove operational support for a production remote database. New rule-specific and final checkpoint validation remains pending.

1.5 branch paths (not maintenance files): `lib/repo/identity.mjs`, `lib/repo/outbox.mjs`, `lib/db/dialect/sqlite.mjs`, `lib/db/dialect/postgres.mjs`, `lib/db/dialect/mssql.mjs`, `lib/identity/secrets.mjs`, `lib/audit/index.mjs`.
